doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Baseball and getting music out of his head
summary: He always hears music; his escape is baseball and PlayStation baseball.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I think you’re doing fine and I’m envious that you’re bilingual. Do you always have music in your head?
Is there a thing you do if you feel like you need to not have it in your head for a while? Is there anything that you do?

Oh yes, oh yes. My real passion is baseball. I’m a frustrated baseball player. I’m a frustrated baseball player, and I know a lot about baseball. So when I want to get out of the world I don’t watch baseball too much anymore because the things that have been happening in baseball for the past few years, the Houston Astros kind of really bothered me a lot. But anyway, I have a playstation full, and I play baseball with my playstation and I go out of the world. Because you know you can play 162 games, the game — keep the stats, and so it’s very good. So that’s my passion. That’s a secret I want to share. I change, I change everything I have done in music [gap] possibility of [gap] © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
